Selection too long — select just the line with the time
Long-press a time (e.g. \"5pm CT\") in any messaging app, pick TimeTwister from the selection menu, and your zones get appended inline.
Rewrite a time into every zone your group cares about, without leaving the chat.
Pick your zones below — every stamp includes them.
In any messaging app, type a time like \"5pm CT\", \"17:00 ET\" or \"5:30pm pacific\".
Long-press the phrase to select it.
Tap the ⋮ overflow in the selection toolbar — TimeTwister is in there, not on the first row.
Tap TimeTwister. The selection becomes \"5pm CT (6pm ET · 3pm PT)\".
TimeTwister almost never appears on the first row of the selection toolbar. Tap the ⋮ to find it.
On someone else\'s message the text can\'t be edited, so TimeTwister copies the converted time to your clipboard and shows it instead.
Illustration of a text selection toolbar: Copy, Paste, Share, then an overflow button that reveals TimeTwister.
Type anything with a time in it
No time detected yet — try \"5pm CT\", \"17:00 ET\" or \"noon\".
This is exactly what TimeTwister would splice into your message.
No target zones. Stamps will re-render the time but add no conversions.
%1$d zones makes the stamp long enough to be unreadable inline. %2$d or fewer keeps it skimmable.
Reads country codes from your contacts to suggest zones. Numbers don\'t leave the device.
Based on country codes in your contacts. Tap to add — already-added zones are skipped.
None of your contacts have international country codes we could match. You can add zones manually.
TimeTwister reads only the country code of each phone number to guess which zones your people are in. It never uploads anything. Without it, add zones by hand — the app works exactly the same.
Android won\'t ask again because contacts access was denied twice. You can turn it on in system settings, or just add zones by hand — the app works exactly the same.
Nothing matches \"%1$s\". Try a city name, a country, or an abbreviation like PT.
